github.name: GitHub
github.title: Everything GitHub ships, on one map
github.description: Products, features, tools, services, programs, learning resources, and agentic development across GitHub.

items.name: GitHub Copilot
items.description: AI coding assistant across IDEs, CLI, app, github.com, and Mobile. GHEC customers can get Copilot for all licensed users; Copilot Business, Enterprise, and Standalone plans are available.

universe.note: GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team get Copilot for every licensed user, with usage metered against the enterprise budget. Users without an Enterprise license can get Copilot Standalone; features match Copilot Enterprise but without monthly AI credits per seat, and Copilot Business and Enterprise stay available.

items.name: Copilot app
items.description: A dedicated desktop workspace for parallel agent tasks, multiple repositories, and the issue-to-pull-request workflow.

items.name: Copilot CLI
items.description: Plan, edit, run commands, and collaborate with a coding agent from your terminal.

items.name: Copilot in IDEs
items.description: Copilot in VS Code and JetBrains: Fusion model option, session continuity with cloud sessions, Agent Host (VS Code), Copilot harness default, GA local sandboxes and next edit suggestions in JetBrains.

universe.note: Universe ’26 added session continuity and Agent Host, alongside new model, tool, and customization integrations.

items.name: Copilot in the cloud
items.description: Ask questions, plan changes, and delegate repository work on GitHub.com and Mobile. Supported sessions can continue across local and cloud clients.

items.name: Microsoft Copilot SDK
items.description: SDK for embedding the Copilot agent runtime in your own apps. Renamed from GitHub Copilot SDK; the repo moves to Microsoft's org in phases while existing package names and docs stay unchanged for now.

universe.note: The GitHub Copilot SDK is being renamed Microsoft Copilot SDK, with the repository moving to the Microsoft organization in phases. Existing package names and docs still say GitHub Copilot SDK and users see no immediate change.

items.name: Copilot Spaces
items.description: Organize and share relevant context so Copilot can answer questions grounded in your team's material.

items.name: Copilot automations
items.description: Prompt, trigger, and tool workflows that run in the cloud. Now shareable with repo collaborators, with REST API and 24 new triggers, chaining, 20 new tools plus custom MCP, credit limits, and self-improvement.

universe.note: Universe ’26 added shared team workflows, VS Code management, learning from outcomes, more triggers and tools, and credit controls.

items.name: Copilot Fusion
items.description: Model-picker option that routes and orchestrates models per task (Single, Cascade, Critique workflows) at Standard, High, or Max effort. Replaces Auto; admins control the model set. Experimental local-model routing.

universe.note: Copilot Fusion is a model-picker option that routes and orchestrates models per task using Single, Cascade, or Critique workflows at Standard, High, or Max effort. It merges Project HydraFusion with auto model selection and replaces Auto; admins control the model set and can make it the default.

items.name: Copilot projects
items.description: Project workspace in the Copilot app that brings work across multiple repositories and sources into one place, with project-level automations. Not the same as GitHub Projects (planning boards).

universe.note: Adds Copilot projects (public preview), a single home for work spanning multiple repos and sources, with project automations. Also adds connected tools such as Slack and Figma, image generation in chat, and computer use (public preview on macOS and Windows) that lets Copilot operate desktop apps with approval.

items.name: Copilot computer use
items.description: Lets Copilot in the app read content, click controls, and enter text across desktop apps, including those without an API, CLI, or MCP. Needs user approval; orgs can disable it via managed settings.

universe.note: Adds Copilot projects (public preview), a single home for work spanning multiple repos and sources, with project automations. Also adds connected tools such as Slack and Figma, image generation in chat, and computer use (public preview on macOS and Windows) that lets Copilot operate desktop apps with approval.

items.name: GitHub intelligence
items.description: Context and learning layer over GitHub's data graph that gives Copilot repository, code, and history context: Copilot Memory (GA), dreaming (preview), and code/semantic search.

universe.note: GitHub intelligence is the context and learning layer over GitHub's data graph. It covers Copilot Memory (GA on paid plans across app, CLI, VS Code, cloud agent, code review, Slack, Teams, and Mobile), Copilot dreaming (opt-in public preview), and code and semantic search used by Copilot.

items.name: Copilot Memory
items.description: Copilot remembers preferences and repository context across sessions and surfaces (app, CLI, VS Code, cloud agent, code review, Slack, Teams, Mobile). GA on paid Copilot plans.

universe.note: GitHub intelligence is the context and learning layer over GitHub's data graph. It covers Copilot Memory (GA on paid plans across app, CLI, VS Code, cloud agent, code review, Slack, Teams, and Mobile), Copilot dreaming (opt-in public preview), and code and semantic search used by Copilot.

items.name: Copilot dreaming
items.description: Opt-in process that reflects on past Copilot work to improve future agent sessions: curates personal memory and tunes repository and code review customization.

universe.note: GitHub intelligence is the context and learning layer over GitHub's data graph. It covers Copilot Memory (GA on paid plans across app, CLI, VS Code, cloud agent, code review, Slack, Teams, and Mobile), Copilot dreaming (opt-in public preview), and code and semantic search used by Copilot.

items.name: Copilot plugins
items.description: Installable bundles of Copilot customizations for VS Code, CLI, and the app. Repos can set a marketplace and default plugins; enterprises can require or block plugins and restrict marketplaces.

universe.note: Repo maintainers can define a plugin marketplace and default plugins for their repository, and enterprises can require or block plugins and restrict marketplaces. Available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app.

items.name: Copilot image generation
items.description: Generate and edit images by prompt in Copilot chat (VS Code, app, CLI) with inline preview and saving to your project. Billed in image tokens against AI credits; admins can disable via model policies.

universe.note: Copilot chat in VS Code, the Copilot app, and CLI can generate and edit images from natural language using an image-generation tool (GPT Image 2.5 Flare), preview them inline, and save them to the project. It is billed in image tokens against AI credits, can be disabled via model policies, and offers an opt-in Made with AI watermark.

items.name: Copilot connectors
items.description: GitHub-verified MCP servers for 26 services (Slack, Figma, Notion, Sentry, Linear, and more). Connect once and use across the Copilot app, CLI, VS Code, cloud agent, and Mobile.

universe.note: GitHub-verified MCP servers, called connectors, launch with 26 services including Slack, Figma, Notion, Sentry, Linear, Atlassian Rovo, Cloudflare, and Vercel. You connect once and use them across the app, CLI, VS Code, cloud agent, and Mobile; Business and Enterprise admins must enable the Editor preview features policy.

items.name: Copilot cloud sandboxes
items.description: Secure cloud environments on GitHub-managed infrastructure where each Copilot cloud session runs by default; they start fast, snapshot on shutdown, and resume from any surface.

universe.note: Cloud tasks started on github.com, Mobile, CLI, app, VS Code, Slack, or Teams share one session list and can be continued from any surface. Each session runs by default in a cloud sandbox that snapshots on shutdown and resumes later; compute draws on the Actions entitlement, which becomes one pool for builds, sandboxes, and larger runners on Team and Enterprise Cloud.

items.name: Session continuity
items.description: Start a Copilot cloud task on github.com, Mobile, CLI, app, VS Code, Slack, or Teams and continue the same session on another surface; every surface shows the same session list.

universe.note: Cloud tasks started on github.com, Mobile, CLI, app, VS Code, Slack, or Teams share one session list and can be continued from any surface. Each session runs by default in a cloud sandbox that snapshots on shutdown and resumes later; compute draws on the Actions entitlement, which becomes one pool for builds, sandboxes, and larger runners on Team and Enterprise Cloud.

items.name: Replica
items.description: Open-source AI prototyping tool from GitHub Design that turns ideas into interactive prototypes using your own design system, used from the Copilot app; optional self-hosted Replica Hub for sharing.

universe.note: GitHub Design open-sourced Replica, an AI prototyping tool that turns ideas into interactive prototypes using your own design system and is used from the Copilot app. An optional self-hosted Replica Hub supports sharing and comments.

items.name: Copilot custom instructions
items.description: Tailor Copilot responses to your preferences, project conventions, and organization requirements with repository, path, personal, and organization instructions.

items.name: Copilot custom agents
items.description: Create specialized agents with tailored expertise for specific development tasks, for Copilot cloud agent (all paid plans) and Copilot CLI.

items.name: Copilot agent skills
items.description: Folders of instructions, scripts, and resources Copilot loads when relevant; work with cloud agent, code review, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code agent mode.

items.name: Copilot hooks
items.description: Run your own shell commands at defined points in an agent's workflow, such as session start or end, prompt entry, or tool calls, for checks and logging.

groups.name: Code & develop
groups.subtitle: Your code and the tools around it

items.name: Repositories
items.description: Store source code, Git history, and documentation in one place, with collaboration and access controls.

items.name: Codespaces
items.description: Configurable cloud development environments built around development containers, available in your browser or supported editors.

items.name: Code search
items.description: Find code with specialized search syntax and navigate symbols and references across repositories.

items.name: github.dev
items.description: A lightweight browser editor for browsing and changing repository files. It is not a compute environment like Codespaces.

items.name: GitHub CLI
items.description: Use the gh command to work with repositories, pull requests, issues, Actions, and GitHub APIs without leaving the terminal.

items.name: GitHub Desktop
items.description: A graphical Git client for reviewing changes, committing, managing branches, and collaborating on repositories.

items.name: GitHub Mobile
items.description: Keep up with notifications, issues, pull requests, and Copilot while away from your development machine.

items.name: Gists
items.description: Share code snippets, notes, and small files as Git-versioned gists, public or secret, at gist.github.com.

items.name: GitHub Projects
items.description: Plan and track work in tables, boards, and roadmaps connected to GitHub issues and pull requests.

items.name: GitHub Issues
items.description: Track bugs and tasks in repositories. The new Moderate role lets users edit and moderate issues and manage labels and milestones without access to code. Issue artifacts are in public preview.

universe.note: A new Moderate repository role lets users edit issues they did not author, transfer, hide, lock, and comment on locked issues, and manage labels, milestones, and discussion categories without code access.

items.name: Discussions
items.description: Host questions, announcements, and open-ended conversations for an open source or internal community.

items.name: Wikis
items.description: Maintain longer-form documentation alongside a repository in a collaborative, versioned wiki.

items.name: Project insights
items.description: Create charts from project data to understand progress and communicate the state of your work.

items.name: Issue artifacts
items.description: Attach Markdown, links, and HTML documents to an issue with version history. Manage them in the UI, with gh issue artifact commands, or via the REST API.

universe.note: Issue artifacts attach Markdown, links, and HTML to an issue, with version history, and can be managed with gh issue artifact commands (create, edit, list, view, download, delete) and a REST API.

items.name: Notifications
items.description: Notification inbox and subscriptions for issues, pull requests, and other activity, delivered on github.com, by email, and in GitHub Mobile.

items.name: Pull requests
items.description: Propose, review, and merge changes. Pull request limits for contributors without write access can now exempt accounts by age or merged-PR history (Moderation > Interaction limits).

universe.note: In Moderation > Interaction limits, pull request limits for contributors without write access can now exempt accounts by minimum age in days or by number of merged PRs in the repo. A contributor is exempt if they meet at least one enabled rule, and repo settings override org settings.

items.name: Copilot code review
items.description: Copilot reviews pull requests. New Max effort (preview) runs multiple review agents across providers with an aggregator; Copilot approvals are GA and count toward required approvals.

universe.note: A new Max review effort level runs multiple independent review agents across model providers plus an aggregator. Copilot approvals are GA, count toward required approvals, and are dismissed on new commits; admins can cap the maximum effort level, and the feature is off by default.

items.name: Stacked pull requests
items.description: Split a larger change into a chain of smaller, dependent pull requests that can be reviewed incrementally.

items.name: Repository rulesets
items.description: Apply rules to branches, tags, and pushes, including requirements for reviews, status checks, and permitted changes.

items.name: Merge queue
items.description: Check pull requests against the latest target branch and queued changes before merging.

items.name: CODEOWNERS
items.description: Define the people or teams responsible for repository paths and automatically request their reviews.

items.name: Agent Merge
items.description: Copilot watches a pull request and fixes failing Actions workflows and merge conflicts in a cloud environment until it is ready to merge. Also in the Copilot app and VS Code; works with auto-merge.

universe.note: Agent Merge lets Copilot watch a pull request and fix failing Actions workflows and merge conflicts in a cloud development environment, started from a Watch and fix control in the merge box. It was already in the Copilot app and VS Code and can be combined with auto-merge.

items.name: GitHub Actions
items.description: Automate builds, tests, deployments, and repository tasks with event-driven workflows defined alongside your code.

items.name: Agentic Workflows
items.description: Open-source GitHub Next project that compiles Markdown into Actions workflows run by AI agents, with integrity filtering, a network firewall, and safe outputs. GA on github.com Free, Team, and Enterprise.

universe.note: GitHub Agentic Workflows, an open source GitHub Next project that compiles Markdown into Actions workflows run by agents, is GA on github.com for Free, Team, and Enterprise. GA adds ARC with Docker-in-Docker support, gh aw forecast, a model router, and micro-VM isolation; the default CLI engine needs a Copilot license.

items.name: Workflow runners
items.description: GitHub-hosted, larger, and self-hosted runners for Actions. Eligible Linux hosted jobs may now run on AWS as well as Azure, so update IP allowlists from the meta API; GHEC opts in via policy.

universe.note: Eligible 2-core and 4-core Linux hosted jobs, and compatible larger runners, may now run on AWS in addition to Azure. It is automatic for Free, Pro, and Team; Enterprise Cloud is opt-in via the Hosted compute cloud providers policy, and IP allowlists should be updated from GET /meta.

items.name: GitHub Packages
items.description: Publish and consume packages alongside your code, including container images through GitHub's Container registry.

items.name: GitHub Pages
items.description: Host static websites directly from a GitHub repository, including documentation and project sites.

items.name: Releases
items.description: Publish tagged versions of a project with release notes and downloadable assets.

items.name: Deployment environments
items.description: Scope deployment secrets and variables and apply protection rules, such as approvals, where supported by your plan.

items.name: Artifact attestations
items.description: Generate and verify provenance records that connect build artifacts to the workflow and source that produced them.

items.name: Workflow lockfiles
items.description: gh actions-lock generates .github/workflows/actions.lock, pinning actions and their transitive dependencies. Dependabot regenerates entries; a Require lockfile policy enforces use.

universe.note: The gh actions-lock CLI extension generates .github/workflows/actions.lock pinning actions and their transitive dependencies. Dependabot can regenerate lock entries and a Require lockfile policy can enforce their use.

items.name: Immutable releases
items.description: Releases whose assets and associated Git tag cannot be changed after publication, blocking tampering with published release artifacts.

groups.name: Security & quality
groups.subtitle: Find risk and fix it in the workflow

items.name: GitHub Code Security
items.description: A GitHub Advanced Security product for finding and fixing vulnerabilities, including code scanning, dependency review, and premium Dependabot capabilities.

items.name: Secret Protection
items.description: Secret scanning and push protection for repos. AI-detected secrets (public preview) let push protection block credentials with no predefined pattern; off by default and uses AI credits.

universe.note: An AI classifier built with Microsoft Applied Sciences lets push protection block secrets that have no known format. It is off by default, requires AI-detected secrets alongside push protection, and consumes AI credits.

items.name: Dependabot
items.description: Automated dependency alerts and update PRs. Reachability analysis (public preview, JS/TS) uses a CodeQL call graph to mark alerts Reachable, Potentially reachable, Unreachable, or Unavailable.

universe.note: A CodeQL call graph labels Dependabot alerts Reachable, Potentially reachable, Unreachable, or Unavailable for JavaScript and TypeScript. It is off by default, never auto-dismisses alerts, and is free on Enterprise Cloud during the preview.

items.name: CodeQL
items.description: Analyze code to find vulnerabilities and errors. CodeQL powers GitHub code scanning and can also run through its CLI.

items.name: Copilot Autofix
items.description: Copilot Autofix for code scanning. Agentic autofix (GA) lets you assign an alert to Copilot, which fixes it, reruns CodeQL, and opens a draft PR for up to 25 alerts.

universe.note: You can assign a code scanning alert to Copilot, which explores the code, fixes it, reruns CodeQL, and opens a draft PR covering up to 25 alerts. It needs the Agentic autofix enterprise policy and consumes AI credits and Actions minutes.

items.name: GitHub Code Quality
items.description: Identify code quality issues before merge and track code health across repositories and teams.

items.name: Security campaigns
items.description: Group security alerts into coordinated remediation campaigns across repositories.

items.name: Security overview
items.description: Review security coverage, risks, trends, and configurations across organizations and repositories.

items.name: Copilot security extension
items.description: GitHub security extension for the Copilot app: browse, explain, fix, and dismiss code scanning alerts, with fixes kept in your local working copy, and run /security-review on local changes.

universe.note: The GitHub security extension for the Copilot app lets you browse, explain, fix, and dismiss code scanning alerts, with fixes applied to your local working copy, and run /security-review on local changes. Install with copilot plugin install github-security@awesome-copilot; not supported on GHES.

items.name: Public monitoring
items.description: Scans public github.com content for leaked secrets attributed to your enterprise by membership or verified domain. Free with Secret Protection on Enterprise Cloud; never scans private repos.

universe.note: Public monitoring scans public github.com content for leaked secrets that belong to your enterprise, attributed by membership or verified domain. It is free with Secret Protection or Advanced Security on Enterprise Cloud, including data residency, and does not scan private repos.

items.name: Code scanning for AI apps
items.description: Pull request code scanning for AI-application risks: indirect prompt injection (XPIA), sensitive information disclosure, and excessive agency. Requires GitHub Advanced Security; not on GHES.

universe.note: Code scanning on pull requests now detects AI-application risks including indirect prompt injection (XPIA), sensitive information disclosure, and excessive agency. It requires GitHub Advanced Security and is not available on GHES.

items.name: GitHub package firewall
items.description: Install-time policy gate between developer endpoints and upstream package registries (npm). Supports a new-version cooldown, Advisory Database checks, and attestation-downgrade checks.

universe.note: A policy gate at install time between developer endpoints and upstream registries, currently for npm. It supports a cooldown on new versions, Advisory Database checks, and attestation-downgrade checks; free during the preview and metered afterward.

items.name: Open source license compliance
items.description: Define an enterprise license policy and enforce it through a ruleset requiring license compliance results before merge. Adds an Enterprise Open-Source License Manager role, audit events, and APIs.

universe.note: Enterprises can define a license policy and enforce it through a ruleset condition that requires license compliance results before merging. It adds an Enterprise Open-Source License Manager role, audit events, and API endpoints.

items.name: AI Scan
items.description: AI-powered security scanning for pull requests (GA) and whole repositories (public preview), covering languages CodeQL does not. Advisory only; results appear as code scanning alerts.

universe.note: AI Scan reviews pull requests for security issues in languages and file types CodeQL does not cover, such as PHP, Shell, Terraform HCL, Dockerfiles, JSP, and Blazor. It is advisory only, does not block merges, and does not run on forks or Dependabot PRs.

items.name: GitHub Advisory Database
items.description: Searchable database of known security vulnerabilities and malware in open source packages, published in OSV format; the source for Dependabot alerts.

items.name: Dependency graph & SBOM
items.description: Maps a repository's dependencies and dependents from manifest and lock files, powers Dependabot alerts, and lets you export a software bill of materials (SBOM).

items.name: Dependency review
items.description: Shows dependency changes in a pull request, with known vulnerabilities and license information, before you merge.

items.name: Private vulnerability reporting
items.description: Lets security researchers privately report vulnerabilities to maintainers of public repositories; maintainers can then draft and publish repository security advisories.

items.name: GitHub Security Lab
items.description: Team of security experts running a collaborative community of developers and security researchers to secure open source software.

items.name: GitHub Bug Bounty
items.description: Public bug bounty program that rewards security researchers for reporting vulnerabilities in GitHub products.

items.name: GitHub Enterprise Cloud
items.description: Hosted GitHub for organizations with SSO, governance, and compliance controls. Now includes Copilot for every licensed user for enterprises with a GitHub or Microsoft account team; usage counts against the budget.

universe.note: GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team get Copilot for every licensed user, with usage metered against the enterprise budget. Users without an Enterprise license can get Copilot Standalone; features match Copilot Enterprise but without monthly AI credits per seat, and Copilot Business and Enterprise stay available.

items.name: Enterprise Server
items.description: Deploy and manage GitHub on infrastructure you control, on premises or in your own cloud environment.

items.name: Data residency
items.description: Use Enterprise Cloud with covered data stored in a supported region. Check the documentation for the exact data and region scope.

items.name: Organizations & teams
items.description: Coordinate people and repositories with shared ownership, roles, and team-based access.

items.name: Enterprise identity
items.description: Connect enterprise identity and access management, including SAML single sign-on and Enterprise Managed Users where supported.

items.name: Audit logs
items.description: Review and export activity records for enterprise administration, security investigations, and governance.

items.name: Billing & usage
items.description: Monitor metered usage and spending, attribute costs, and configure budgets and alerts.

items.name: Copilot usage metrics
items.description: Dashboards and API data that help administrators see how teams adopt Copilot, track engagement, and find enablement opportunities.

items.name: GitHub Expert Services
items.description: Hands-on consulting, guided workshops, and training from the GitHub Expert Services team to help organizations adopt GitHub.

items.name: GitHub Premium Support
items.description: Paid enterprise support plan with 24/7 coverage and dedicated GitHub experts.

items.name: GitHub Connect
items.description: Connects a GitHub Enterprise Server instance to your Enterprise Cloud enterprise to share selected data and workflows.

items.name: GitHub Marketplace
items.description: Discover apps and Actions that extend GitHub and connect development workflows to other tools.

items.name: REST & GraphQL APIs
items.description: Query GitHub data and automate workflows with its REST and GraphQL APIs; use webhooks to respond to events.

items.name: GitHub Apps
items.description: Build integrations with fine-grained permissions, installation-based access, and webhook events.

items.name: GitHub MCP server
items.description: Give compatible AI tools access to GitHub capabilities through the Model Context Protocol, subject to authentication and permissions.

items.name: GitHub Education
items.description: Learning and teaching resources, classroom tools, and eligible student and educator benefits.

items.name: GitHub Sponsors
items.description: Fund open source contributors and projects, or receive financial support for eligible open source work.

items.name: GitHub Support
items.description: Get help with GitHub products through the support channels included with your plan, with additional Premium Support options.

items.name: Migration tools
items.description: Move repositories and supported project data to GitHub or between GitHub products using migration tooling.

items.name: npm registry
items.description: The npm public package registry and CLI for publishing and installing JavaScript packages; npm is owned by GitHub. Distinct from the npm registry in GitHub Packages.

items.name: GitHub Docs
items.description: Official documentation for GitHub products and features, with guides, concepts, and reference for each plan and product.

items.name: GitHub Status
items.description: Real-time GitHub service status with incident updates and email, SMS, and other subscription options.

items.name: GitHub Community
items.description: Community discussion forum for questions, feature feedback, and announcements from GitHub staff and users.

items.name: GitHub Partner Program
items.description: Partner programs for Technology, Service and Channel, Startups, and Education partners, with co-branding and specialist guidance.

items.name: GitHub Secure Open Source Fund
items.description: Funding program powered by GitHub Sponsors that pays maintainers of fast-growing open source dependencies to improve security, with expert guidance and emergency support.

items.name: GitHub Stars
items.description: Program that recognizes and supports community leaders who educate and inspire developers.

items.name: GitHub Archive Program
items.description: Initiative to preserve open source software for future generations, including the Arctic Code Vault snapshot.

items.name: GitHub Next
items.description: GitHub's research and engineering team that prototypes future developer tools; origin of Agentic Workflows.

items.name: Profiles
items.description: Personal profile pages that show your repositories, contributions, and activity, and can be customized.

items.name: Webhooks
items.description: Receive HTTP callbacks when events occur on GitHub, to integrate with external services and automate workflows.

items.name: Trending
items.description: See which repositories and developers the GitHub community is most excited about today, filterable by language.

groups.name: Learn & practice
groups.subtitle: Build GitHub and Copilot skills hands-on

items.name: GitHub Skills
items.description: Hands-on, repository-based courses for Git, GitHub, pull requests, Actions, and more. Learn by completing practical exercises in real GitHub workflows.

items.name: Microsoft Learn for GitHub
items.description: GitHub learning paths from Microsoft Learn, including GitHub Foundations and Copilot modules on prompt engineering, agent mode, cloud Copilot, and MCP.

azure.name: Azure AI
azure.title: Azure AI and agents, on one map
azure.description: A focused guide to Microsoft Foundry, agent frameworks, models, grounding, safety, and AI learning. General Azure infrastructure is intentionally out of scope.

groups.name: Agents & orchestration
groups.subtitle: Build, connect, and operate AI agents

items.name: Microsoft Foundry
items.description: Unified platform for building and managing AI applications and agents, with models, tools, evaluations, tracing, governance, and enterprise controls.

items.name: Foundry Agent Service
items.description: Managed runtime for building, deploying, and scaling prompt and hosted agents with model access, tools, identities, and lifecycle management.

items.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description: Open-source SDK for building agents and multi-agent workflows across model providers, tools, MCP servers, memory, and hosting options.

items.name: Foundry Toolboxes
items.description: Curate tools once and expose them through a shared MCP-compatible endpoint with centralized credentials, governance, observability, and versioning.

items.name: Agent routines
items.description: Run Foundry agents automatically on schedules or events, with permissions, connections, and run history managed alongside the agent.

items.name: Agent-to-agent (A2A)
items.description: Connect agents across frameworks and services so they can discover one another and coordinate work through the A2A protocol.

items.name: MCP for Foundry agents
items.description: Connect Foundry agents and toolboxes to remote MCP servers, with authentication and centralized tool configuration.

items.name: Long-running hosted agents
items.description: Keep agent work running after a client disconnects and recover it after process restarts with durable task identity, persisted inputs, and stream replay.

items.name: Azure skill for Microsoft Foundry
items.description: A reusable agent skill covering Foundry model deployment, agent development, routines, A2A, evaluation, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

groups.name: Models & inference
groups.subtitle: Choose, route, and run AI models

items.name: Microsoft Foundry Models
items.description: Discover, compare, evaluate, and deploy models from Microsoft, Azure OpenAI, and partner or community providers through one catalog.

items.name: Foundry Model Router
items.description: Route each prompt to a suitable model in real time, balancing quality, cost, and latency through a single model deployment.

items.name: Foundry Local
items.description: Run generative AI models locally for low-latency, offline-capable applications, including assistants, search, translation, speech, and vision.

items.name: Azure AI Search
items.description: AI-ready search and retrieval, including vector and hybrid search and agentic retrieval, to ground models and agents in enterprise content.

items.name: Foundry IQ
items.description: Managed knowledge layer built on Azure AI Search that turns enterprise content into permission-aware knowledge bases for agents.

items.name: Azure Document Intelligence
items.description: Extract text, tables, key-value pairs, and structured fields from forms and documents to prepare content for AI applications and agents.

items.name: Azure Content Understanding
items.description: Use generative AI to analyze documents, images, video, and audio, then transform unstructured content into structured, searchable data.

items.name: Foundry evaluations
items.description: Measure model and agent quality, safety, and reliability with datasets, simulations, production traces, and built-in or custom evaluators.

items.name: Foundry observability
items.description: Trace and monitor AI applications and agents across development and production, with quality, safety, performance, and operational signals.

items.name: Azure AI Content Safety
items.description: Detect harmful user- and AI-generated content and apply guardrails to models, agents, and applications.

groups.name: Learn & build
groups.subtitle: Get hands-on with Azure AI agents

items.name: Develop AI agents on Azure
items.description: Microsoft Learn path for developing AI agents with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service and Microsoft Agent Framework, including multi-agent orchestration.

items.name: Microsoft Foundry capability map
items.description: Official map of Microsoft Foundry capabilities across agents, tools, knowledge, evaluation, observability, trust, and model operations.
